set.def: so small or slight that it does not matter or is not worth considering
perfectly clean and neat, with no marks, dirt, or mistakes
clever and original, especially in finding a new way to solve a problem

set.def: stating opinions openly and boldly, even when they may upset or anger others
so silly or unreasonable that it makes people laugh at it
strange or mysterious in a way that is hard to explain and often slightly disturbing
too pleased with yourself and your achievements, in a way that other people find unpleasant
able to express ideas clearly and well, in a way that moves or convinces people, especially in speech
quick to understand situations and people accurately and to use this to your advantage
firmly determined to do something and not willing to give up or change your mind
definitely and clearly; to a degree that is obvious to everyone
in a way that is widely known for something bad
in a very obvious way, without any attempt to hide it, usually about something wrong
in a strong, passionate, and intense way, especially when disagreeing
in an unsure or careful way, or as a plan that is not yet final
to escape from or avoid something or someone, often by using clever tricks
a time of serious trouble or bad luck that is hard to deal with

set.also: to treat someone or something as not good enough for you (“She disdained their offer of help.”)
set.def: the feeling that someone or something is not good enough to deserve your respect or attention
something that makes people less likely to do something, especially by making them afraid of what will happen
a sudden, violent, or major change that causes great confusion in people's lives
a person who is unfairly blamed for the mistakes or bad actions of others
confused and mixed up, so that it is hard to understand or follow
harmless and unlikely to upset or hurt anyone
behaving as if you are more important than others, often using grand, formal words to impress
full of loud noise, confusion, or sudden violent change; not calm at all

set.def: wicked or criminal, especially through secret, evil plans
lacking energy, brightness, or excitement; dull and boring
very grand or ambitious in a way meant to impress, but often too big to be realistic
tired, bored, and no longer excited after having or doing too much of something
extremely pleasant, peaceful, and beautiful, like a perfect scene from a painting or story
to deeply respect and admire someone or something
to make someone feel isolated or turn against you, often so that you lose their support
to make someone or something seem small, weak, or of little value
anger caused by something that seems unfair or wrong

set.def: skill in handling people or sensitive matters without upsetting or hurting anyone
a strong liking for something or a tendency to do it often
a feeling of being too satisfied with things as they are, so that possible dangers or problems are ignored
extreme pride or self-confidence, especially the kind that leads a person to fail or be punished
without knowing or realizing what one is doing; not on purpose
in a way that seems to go against itself or is the opposite of what you would expect

set.also: a person who stays in a place only for a short time before moving on (“The shelter offers beds to transients.”)
likely to start arguments with other people (“He was a contentious man who argued with everyone.”)

why: also format; peaceful not an opposite of a disputed issue

set.also: able to be felt by touching, especially of something in the body (“The doctor found a palpable lump.”)
a long, firm pillow (“She propped herself up on a bolster.”)
the care and teaching a child gets while growing up (“Is talent shaped more by nature or nurture?”)
a Christian holy day held on January 6 (“Many churches hold a special service at Epiphany.”)
only slightly warm; neither hot nor cold (“The coffee had gone lukewarm.”)
relating to a local church and its area, or run by a local church (“She went to a parochial school.”)
a nation or group that is fighting in a war (“Both belligerents agreed to a ceasefire.”)
able to burn or eat away things by chemical action (“Wear gloves when using caustic drain cleaners.”)
to die from an illness or injury (“He succumbed to his wounds.”)
to make it hard for someone to breathe (“The heat in the crowded room was stifling.”)
to say that something is not true; deny (“No evidence could negate her claim.”)
the act of catching and arresting someone (“The reward led to the apprehension of the suspect.”)
a pointed end where two curves meet, such as the point on a tooth (“Each molar has several cusps.”)
a physical problem that makes speaking hard (“He has a mild speech impediment.”)
in chess, a position where a player cannot make a legal move but is not in check, so the game is a draw (“The chess game ended in stalemate.”)

why: doubtfully means 'with doubt', not a true opposite
ignore is not a true opposite of think carefully
'deal' in this sense not recognizable as a synonym
dawdle is not the same meaning
allure is attractiveness, not the same meaning
caprice obscure; plan is not a true opposite
passivity is not the same meaning
ideal means perfect, not most typical
gist is the general idea, not the key point
